stocks.note: Numbers as of market close April 28th.
stocks.news:
Markets slid into Fed Day. Spotify (SPOT -12.43%) tanked on weak Q2 premium subscriber guidance (299M vs. 300M expected); the company has hiked U.S. Prices twice in two years and may be running out of pricing room.

GM (GM +1.27%) beat estimates partly thanks to a $500M tariff refund, but warned of $1.1B in fresh EV charges. Total EV pullback is now near $8.7B.

Jamie Dimon (JPM -0.05%) publicly warned of a possible bond crisis and a recession "worse than people think." Add today's Fed announcement to that backdrop.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET April 28th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
WTI ripped +6.7% to $106.62, the biggest single-day move in months. The catalyst: UAE announced exit from OPEC May 1 after 59 years, and Ryanair flagged airline failure risk if jet fuel holds at $150/barrel through summer. Brent topped $111.

The 10-year sat flat ahead of today's Fed announcement, but the bond market's calm masks the inflation re-emergence in the oil tape. Gold ticked down marginally off record highs.

46% of 2025 retirees stopped working earlier than planned per a new survey, with 76% citing reasons outside their control (health, layoffs, caregiving). Translation: "work longer" is the most popular retirement plan, and it fails nearly half the time. That's a slow-burn driver for downsizer listings over the next 24 months.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on April 28th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto continued its pullback. Galaxy Digital (GLXY +5.23%) posted a $216M Q1 loss (after $482M last quarter) as crypto values dropped 20% YTD, but its Helios data center went live this month to start earning AI compute revenue. The rotation from mining to AI hosting is now real.

On the regulatory front, the CFTC is rolling out AI tools to screen crypto firm license applications while cutting 20%+ of its staff. Faster approvals for legitimate crypto firms is the upshot.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates Snap Higher on Oil Surge; Fed Decides Today
real_estate.commentary:
The mortgage rate ceiling we've been watching just got pushed up. 30-year is 6.45% (up 13bp), 15-year crossed back to 6.00%, both moving with WTI ripping +6.7% to $106.62 and Brent past $111. The driver: UAE announced it's leaving OPEC May 1 after 59 years (wants to pump more, but the breakup is pricing in as supply chaos), and Ryanair's CEO warned European airlines could fail at $150/barrel jet fuel. Rates follow oil, oil is following geopolitics, and the Fed announces today (Wednesday) into all of it.

The cross-currents going into the meeting: BofA just raised 2026 GDP to 2.8% (cuts harder), consumer confidence at all-time low (cuts urgent), now oil pushing inflation back into the conversation. Jamie Dimon warned yesterday of a potential "bond crisis" if government debt keeps climbing and called a recession "worse than people think." That's exactly the dynamic playing out in mortgage rates this morning.

One bright spot for Bay Area listings: the office-demand index just hit its highest level since the pandemic, with San Francisco leading the rebound alongside NY and LA, driven by AI, tech, finance, and law firms. If SF tech keeps absorbing seats, Tri-Valley commuter housing demand has a real tailwind.
